evals.prompt: Find me a recent paper on retrieval augmented generation for reducing hallucination in code review comments, and let's discuss it against my idea of using RAG over a project's own commit history to ground review suggestions.
evals.expected_output: Asks which provider(s) to search before running any provider search, presents a short ranked list without fetching full text yet, confirms which single paper to open, then delegates fetching to document-reader, discusses it against the user's stated idea, and records a discussion note via research_notes_create/update.
expectations: Asks via AskUserQuestion which of arXiv / Europe PMC / both to search before calling any provider search tool
Presents a ranked list of candidates before fetching any full text
Confirms with the user which single paper to open before dispatching document-reader
Delegates the initial fetch to the document-reader subagent rather than calling fetch/parse tools directly from the main thread
Discussion explicitly relates the paper's claims, method, or limitations to the user's stated RAG-over-commit-history idea
Runs the find-or-create note flow (research_notes_search, then create or update) after the discussion automatically, without asking the user whether to save it
Does not draft, outline, or write manuscript prose at any point

evals.prompt: I have this paper: arXiv 2401.12345v2. Let's talk about whether its evaluation methodology is sound compared to what I'm doing in my thesis on federated learning privacy.
evals.expected_output: Skips search/select since the identifier is already given, dispatches document-reader for the initial fetch, and discusses the paper's methodology only in relation to the user's stated thesis topic, dispatching document-reader again for any specific textual detail needed.
expectations: Does not perform a search step since a specific identifier was already provided
Dispatches document-reader for the initial Fetch rather than calling research_arxiv_fetch_full_text/parse_full_text directly from the main thread
Discussion of evaluation methodology is grounded only in the paper's actual text, not invented details
Any specific textual detail needed mid-discussion is obtained via a fresh document-reader dispatch, not by the main thread claiming to already hold the full text
Does not pull any other paper's full text into the discussion

evals.prompt: Can you help me discuss this Europe PMC paper PMC1234567 about CRISPR off-target effects? I'm building a similar off-target prediction model and want to know how their validation compares to mine.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches document-reader to fetch via the Europe PMC XML-only pair, and if full text isn't available, offers to discuss from abstract/metadata only instead of failing silently or substituting a web fetch.
expectations: Dispatches document-reader for the fetch rather than calling research_europepmc_fetch_full_text/parse_full_text from the main thread
If document-reader reports full text unavailable (format_unavailable), explicitly offers to continue from abstract/metadata only rather than silently stopping
Never substitutes a built-in web search/fetch tool for the prioris-mcp calls

evals.prompt: This paper has three existing discussion notes already (topics: evaluation, related-work, limitations). Add a new point about their ablation study's statistical significance to the discussion.
evals.expected_output: Searches for existing skill:discuss notes on this paper, presents the three existing topics plus a start-new option via AskUserQuestion, and updates or creates based on the user's pick rather than guessing which topic the ablation point belongs to.
expectations: Calls research_notes_search scoped to this paper and skill:discuss before deciding where to write
Presents the existing topics via AskUserQuestion using format_note_choices.py-style deterministic labels rather than an LLM-authored summary
Includes a start-a-new-topic option alongside the existing ones
Does not use tag closeness alone to silently pick a topic without asking
Calls research_notes_update on the picked note (tags untouched) or research_notes_create for a new topic, matching the user's choice
